questions.q: When a number is typed in a cell, Excel aligns it to the —
questions.solution: **Numbers right-align, text left-aligns** automatically — a quick test of what Excel thinks your data is.

questions.q: Keeping backup copies of files on **internet servers** so they are reachable anywhere is called —
questions.solution: **Cloud backup** copies your data to remote servers over the internet — accessible from any device with a login.

questions.q: To jump directly to slide 15 during a show, press —
questions.solution: **Number + Enter** teleports the show to that slide number.

questions.q: Malware that hides deep in a system and conceals its own presence while giving an attacker administrator-level access is a —
questions.solution: **Rootkit** = root (admin) + kit — hides itself and hands over admin control.

questions.q: Select the word which is nearest in meaning to the given word.  ENERVATE
questions.solution: **Enervate** = to drain of strength = weaken. It looks like 'energy' but points the other way; 'energise' is the planted trap.

questions.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
questions.solution: After the helper **did**, the base form is required: part 2 must be **end** ('did the lecture end'). The no-sooner…than frame in parts 3 and 4 is correctly built.
questions.shortcut: did + base verb; than pairs with no sooner.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  The list of candidates ___ been published.
questions.solution: The head noun is **list** (singular); the of-phrase does not change it → has been published.

questions.q: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution: **Achievement** = achieve + ment. The pair makes an 'ee' sound after h (not c), so it is **ie**, and the e of achieve stays before the consonant suffix -ment.
questions.shortcut: No c before the 'ee' pair -> ie; achieve keeps its e.

questions.q: The five-kingdom classification of living organisms was proposed by:
questions.solution: **R.H. Whittaker** proposed the five kingdoms — Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia — in **1969**. Linnaeus gave binomial nomenclature and the two-kingdom system.
questions.shortcut: My Pet Fish Plays Alone — Whittaker.

questions.q: A nutcracker is an example of which class of lever?
questions.solution: In a nutcracker the **load (nut) lies between** the hinge (fulcrum) and the hands (effort), making it a **class 2** lever, like a wheelbarrow and a bottle opener.

questions.q: Which of the following is **NOT** one of the seven SI base units?
questions.solution: The base units are metre, kilogram, second, ampere, kelvin, mole and candela. The **newton** is derived: 1 N = 1 kg·m/s².
questions.shortcut: Named after a person but not in the 7-list = derived (only kelvin and ampere are both).

questions.q: The **First Five Year Plan** (1951-56) was based on the —
questions.solution: The 1st plan used the **Harrod-Domar** growth model and gave top priority to agriculture and irrigation — a success thanks to good monsoons.

questions.q: If $x+y=5$ and $x^2+y^2=13$, then $x^4+y^4$ is equal to:
Which term of the HP $\dfrac{1}{9}, \dfrac{1}{14}, \dfrac{1}{19}, \ldots$ is $\dfrac{1}{54}$?
questions.solution:
Reciprocals: 9, 14, 19, ... ($d = 5$).
$9 + (n-1)5 = 54 \Rightarrow n = 10$.

questions.q: The maximum value of $\sin\theta\cos\theta$ ($\theta$ acute) is:
questions.solution: $\sin\theta\cos\theta = \frac{\sin 2\theta}{2} \le \frac12$, at $\theta = 45^\circ$.
questions.shortcut: $\frac12$ at $45^\circ$. Trap: $1$ — that is the max of $2\sin\theta\cos\theta$, not of the product.

questions.q: The difference between the compound interest and the simple interest on a sum for 3 years at 10% per annum is ₹310. The sum is:
questions.shortcut: Using the 2-year formula gives ₹31,000 — count 3 years here.

questions.q: In the **evening**, Ramesh's shadow falls **exactly in front of him**. Which direction is he facing?
questions.solution: Evening sun is in the West, so shadows point **East**. A shadow in front means he faces along it → **East**.
questions.shortcut: Evening shadow = East; 'in front' ⇒ facing the shadow's direction.

questions.q: In a class test, **Mohan ranks 13th from the top and 57th from the bottom.** How many students appeared for the test?
questions.shortcut: a + b − 1, then sanity-check a + b = n + 1.

questions.q:
Select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series.

**6, 12, 20, 30, 42, ?**
questions.shortcut: Product of two consecutive numbers — differences are 6, 8, 10, 12, 14.
